Name: nn_architecture_impact
Title: Neural Network Architecture Impact on Orbit Correction Accuracy
Experiment: Compare orbit correction performance (L₂ residual) of different neural network architectures (Dense, CNN, LSTM) trained on identical datasets. Evaluate sensitivity to hidden parameter variations and computational efficiency.

Name: data_scaling_effect
Title: Training Data Scaling Effects on ML Correction Robustness
Experiment: Quantify orbit correction improvement when increasing training samples (100→1000) and tightening optimization tolerance (1e-8→1e-10). Measure generalization to unseen σψ variations.

Name: hybrid_correction
Title: Hybrid SVD-Neural Network Correction Framework
Experiment: Develop cascade system: SVD coarse correction followed by NN residual optimization. Compare pure NN/SVD against hybrid approach in computational cost and orbit minimization.

Name: online_adaptation
Title: Online Adaptation of Neural Corrector via Transfer Learning
Experiment: Implement real-time NN fine-tuning using transfer learning when accelerator configuration drifts. Measure steps required to adapt to new σₓ/σᵧ regimes without full retraining.

Name: uncertainty_quantification
Title: Uncertainty Quantification in NN-Based Orbit Prediction
Experiment: Incorporate Monte Carlo dropout in neural network to estimate uncertainty bounds for corrector magnet settings. Validate against MAD-X perturbation analysis.

Name: computational_efficiency_benchmark
Title: Real-Time Computational Efficiency: SVD vs Neural Network Correction
Experiment: Modify correct_orbit() to time full correction cycles (MAD-X calls + computation). Implement NN inference timing. For corrector subsets (10/20/30/36), run 50 trials measuring: 1) Wall-clock time 2) Final orbit residuals. Report 95th percentiles for time and mean residuals per configuration.

Name: optimization_paradigm_comparison
Title: Operational Comparison of Orbit Correction Paradigms Under Extreme Conditions
Experiment: Extend correct_orbit() to implement SVD, L-BFGS-B, and NN approaches with shared constraint handling (±7A). For 50 misalignment configurations (including 3σ+ stress-tests from validation protocol Phase 3), measure: 1) L₂ residuals 2) Maximum displacements 3) Computation time 4) Current usage efficiency (A·m/residual reduction) 5) Beam stability impact via MAD-X lifetime calculations. Perform ANOVA to identify statistically significant performance differences across operational regimes.

Name: girder_misalignment_robustness
Title: Girder-Style Misalignment Robustness and Mitigation Strategies for Orbit Correction
Experiment: Modify VEPP5_sample.start_madx() to assign shared misalignments to element groups (1-5 elements/girder). For 5 group sizes, run 100 trials measuring: 1) L₂ residual vs group size 2) Magnet current requirements 3) Efficacy of adaptive SVD cutoff (1e-3 to 1e-1). Characterize failure thresholds and optimal mitigation parameters.

Name: bpm_failure_resilience
Title: Sensor Failure Resilience Analysis for Accelerator Orbit Correction Systems
Experiment: Modify VEPP5_sample: 1) Add BPM masking in _get_orbit() to completely exclude selected sensors from measurements 2) Adjust calculcate_resp_mat() to compute reduced-dimension response matrices 3) Implement symmetric BPM pair selection based on lattice sectors. For 100 configurations: Run baseline correction (all 16 BPMs), then systematically disable symmetric BPM pairs (4-12 BPMs total). Record L₂ residuals, max displacement, correction stability (iterations to converge), and computation time for both SVD and NN methods. Compute criticality scores per BPM location based on degradation metrics.

Name: strategic_corrector_subsets
Title: Strategic Corrector Subset Selection for Resource-Efficient Orbit Correction
Experiment: Modify VEPP5_sample: 1) Add subset selection to calculcate_resp_mat() and correct_orbit() 2) Compute column norms in response matrix to identify high-leverage correctors 3) Infer physical sectors from corrector names (e.g., 'i_c12'→sector1) 4) Test 6 strategies: a) All 36 correctors b) Top 18 high-leverage c) Top 9 high-leverage d) Sector-based groups (by name) e) Alternating indices f) Random subset. For each: Measure L₂ residuals, max displacement, current variance, computation time, and success rate under ±7A limits across 100 configurations. Determine minimum corrector sets maintaining <1e-4m residuals.
